sections.name: Paper
sections.title: Shape of a research paper entry
sections.what: Describes one published paper: its three versions of the title (formal, calm and technical), venue, conference, dates, location, authors, web link, DOI, and whether the owner was lead author.
sections.why: Keeps every paper in the same format so the research pages can show them the same way.
sections.watch_out: The lead author flag is only yes or no, so it cannot show shared leadership.

sections.name: ResearchThread
sections.title: Shape of a research theme
sections.what: Describes one research theme: its title, a plain description, a technical description and a set of tags.
sections.why: Keeps every theme in the same format.

sections.name: researchThreads
sections.title: The four research themes
sections.what: Lists the four current research themes: multi-agent finance, document intelligence, continuous portfolio intelligence, and career simulation. Each has a plain-language and a technical description.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely the source of the themes shown on the research page.
sections.watch_out: Tags are free text and nothing here checks them, so a typo goes unnoticed.

sections.name: papers (part 1)
sections.title: First three papers from 2015
sections.what: Holds three papers from 2015: one on tether deployment, one on attitude control, and one on tether control. Each has the full author list, conference details, and both descriptions.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely kept as data so the research page can show them without a database.
sections.watch_out: The DOI, date and link fields must match each paper's real record. Nothing here checks them.

sections.name: papers (part 2)
sections.title: Fourth paper and end of list
sections.what: Holds the fourth paper, from 2016, on a ground test set-up for the satellite's control system. It is marked as not lead author, and the list ends here. The entry starts in the previous section.
sections.why: Likely reason: the lead author flag is set to no because the owner was a co-author on this paper.
sections.watch_out: The list is typed by hand, so a new paper must be added inside the square brackets with every field filled in.

summary: Holds the owner's research themes and the list of published papers shown on the research pages, written as plain data.
purpose: Stores the content for the research section so the pages can display it without any calculation.
why: Likely reason: keeping content in data files lets the owner change text without touching page layout. Reason not stated in the code.
how: First, the Paper shape and the ResearchThread shape define the format. Then researchThreads lists four themes. Then papers lists four papers, each with a plain and a technical version of its text, conference details and links.
inputs: Nothing is read from outside. The content is typed directly into this file.
outputs: Two exported lists, researchThreads and papers, which pages import to display research content.
risks: Nothing checks the DOI numbers, dates, links or author names against the real publications. A typo will display without any error. Papers and themes are not validated when the site builds.
debug: If a paper or theme shows wrong text, check its entry in this file first. If a page fails to load, check that every entry has all the required fields. Compare DOIs and links with the publisher's pages.
